title: Cap. X: to avoid calumny — our Church rejects both those who make God cause of unbelief/damnation by absolute antecedent will, and Arminian/Pelagian errors that make each man after common sufficient grace the smith of his own eternal fortune
pass_a_gloss: And here, that we may avoid the calumnies of the malevolent, we are again and again compelled to repeat, that our Church no less rejects the portentous opinions of those who so depict unto us the decree of reprobation that they establish God as the cause of human unbelief and impenitence, and even recall the very perdition and damnation of men unto the absolute and antecedent will of God, than the errors of the Arminians drawn from the dregs of Pelagius, who so propose unto us the decrees of predestination and of reprobation that meanwhile they constitute every one, after the decree concerning administering sufficient grace commonly, as smith of his own fortune in gratuitous and everlasting goods; God namely waiting and looking what men will do, and according as he shall have foreseen them about to believe, or not about to believe, electing them or not electing, that is, reprobating.
pass_b_english: And here, to avoid malevolent calumnies, we must keep repeating: our Church rejects no less those portentous opinions that so paint the reprobation decree as to make God the cause of human unbelief and impenitence, and even refer men's very perdition and damnation to God's absolute antecedent will — than the Arminian errors drawn from Pelagius's dregs, which so set the decrees of predestination and reprobation that after the decree to administer common sufficient grace, each man is made smith of his own fortune in free and everlasting goods. God waits and watches what men will do, and as he foresaw them about to believe or not, elects them or does not elect — that is, reprobates.
source_text: Atque hic, ut vitemus malevolorum calumnias, subinde cogimur repetere, Ecclesiam nostram non minus rejicere portentosas illorum opiniones, qui sic reprobationis decretum nobis depingunt, ut Deum infidelitatis et impoenitentiae humanae causam statuant, ipsamque adeo perditionem et damnationem hominum in Dei absolutam et antecedentem voluntatem revocent, quam Arminianorum ex Pelagii faecibus haustos errores, qui sic praedestinationis et reprobationis decreta nobis proponunt, ut interim unumquemque, post decretum de administranda communiter gratia sufficiente, constituant in gratuitis et aeternis bonis fabrum fortunae suae; Deo scilicet praestolante et intuente quid homines sint facturi, et prout praeviderit eos credituros, aut non credituros, eligente eos vel non eligente, hoc est, reprobante.
